page: Amazon Web Services c6a.12xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro System and 3rd Generation AMD EPYC 7R13 processors running at up to 3.6 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 48 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core complex, supported by instruction set capabilities such as AVX, AES-NI, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2.

System memory consists of 96.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3000 MHz, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring external elastic block storage for persistent filesystem needs. Baseline networking throughput is provisioned at 19 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPUs is not available in this instance family.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing power, with top-tier results in stress-ng CPU tests and PassMark CPU encryption metrics, alongside high performance in ray tracing and image processing routines. Synthetic memory benchmarks show uncached large-block read speeds of 66.3 GB/sec and write speeds of 30.23 GB/sec. Application-level metrics record 52.39 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput of 20.29 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the instance delivers high compute density per allocated core without requiring higher-cost memory or bundled local disk overhead. A clear architectural tradeoff is the absence of local ephemeral storage and the lack of AVX-512 extensions. The server is well aligned with compute-bound workloads, distributed compilation, video and image rendering, batch processing pipelines, and microservices topologies that rely entirely on network-attached storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance built on the Nitro System and powered by AMD EPYC 7R13 processors clocked at 3.6 GHz. Operating on x86_64 architecture, it delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores alongside 96.0 GB of DDR4-3000 RAM, reflecting a compute-focused 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 19 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains zero dedicated GPUs, and does not bundle local storage, relying on network-attached block volumes. Benchmark testing indicates strong results in multi-core CPU computation, cryptographic operations, and image processing, while exhibiting standard DDR4 throughput across uncached memory operations. Because it eliminates the premium of local NVMe storage and large memory banks, c6a.12xlarge provides resource-efficient CPU capacity for batch processing, web fleet tiers, software build pipelines, and compute-intensive distributed applications.
